decisions.reason: The even-page constraint is already owned by flipbook spread compatibility; the digital flipbook PDF deliverable remains valid unchanged.
Page-count parity does not change the free-to-start platform requirement or candidate platform list, and the message does not select a new platform.
The source explicitly applies the even-page requirement to the Flip Book pages version, not the deferred print-ready output.
An even final page count may affect eventual pagination values but does not change the requirement that cover references use accurate final page numbers.
Flipbook page-count parity has no effect on the issue edition or date labels.
The table of contents must already use finalized pagination; requiring an even flipbook page count does not alter that rule.
The page-count constraint does not change the requirement to enhance publication images when necessary.
Flipbook page-count parity does not change category labels, mappings, placement, or allowed categories.
The even-page requirement does not affect author identity, photo matching, source, or placement.
Page-count parity does not change the requirement that advertisements render clearly; the source's separate replacement statement is not part of the parity modification.
The even-page constraint does not modify the existing policy against empty white areas at article endings.
Flipbook page-count parity has no effect on author photo shape or size.
